answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by binding identity to verifiable work plus a refundable stake. Reputation accrues only when peers attest completed tasks — nectar earned only by flowers pollinated. Each identity locks a deposit, slashed if its attestations prove false. An attacker creating thousands of fake agents pays per identity: a separate stake and work history, so each extra fake costs more than it gains. In a tundra of cheap identities the stake is the cold that weeds out fakes, and a delta of trust forms only around agents verified by counterparties.
